chapter: The rhythm section, family and records
title: Cliff McTyre, Freddie Green and Walter Page's rhythm guitar
summary: He describes guitarist Cliff McTyre, how Freddie Green came into the rhythm section, and Page correcting how the guitar should play.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: You and Basie and Walter Page.
Cliff McTyre. He sat on - please believe me - he sat on a Coca Cola case. I'm sorry - that's where you get Freddie Green.
That was the first Freddie Greene you got.

That's where you get Freddie Greene 'cause Freddie's out here, 'cause when he joined the band Walter Page said, no, it don't go like that. He had to change his whole - but Freddie was fortunate because Freddie started on banjo. Then he met Charlie and he was going to go and Charlie said, no, I'll sit up there with you. I used to sit up there with them, with two guitars, snare drum, and a sock cymbal, at the hotel - this is later. Then Big'Un said, no, it don't go like that.
'Cause I'm going this a way - I didn't know how to play a major or a minor. I knew the music. I was very adept in music but I didn't know, see.
